What was wrong: the profiling build's Metal source did not compile, so the program died during startup before tracing a single frame — and my sweep hid the reason.

Details, from my own history (messages #51-#58):
- The PT_PROF shortcuts went into the .metal files, and this program compiles its shaders at startup with newLibraryWithSource, so a shader error is a runtime failure, not a clang failure. The clang++ link succeeded and _prof/pathtracer existed, which is why the first sign was empty output rather than a compile error.
- One guard I wrote used a bare `params` inside a function that has no such local: in pt_trace.metal's scene-intersection helper the parameters are reached through the scene struct, so the line `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && pt_intersect_mesh(...))` failed with "use of undeclared identifier 'params'".
- The host prints "metal init error: shader compile failed: program_source:615:10: error: ..." on stderr and exits without rendering, so it emitted no benchmark line. My sweep loop did `2>/dev/null | tail -1` and echoed "PT_PROF=$P $R", so each line came out as "PT_PROF=0 " with an empty result — six blank results, no error text.
- How I found it: I re-ran a single invocation with stderr shown (message #54), which printed the shader-compile error. I changed that guard to `scene.params->pad` (#55) and re-ran the same loop; since shaders compile at launch, no rebuild was needed and all six variants printed timings (#58): gpu_ms_best 45.352 (full), 44.051 (no shadow walk), 4.773 (no mesh closest-hit), 43.171 (no NEE), 35.764 (glass always-reflect), 0.458 (no shadow + no mesh) — the measurement that put ~89% of the frame in the closest-hit BVH walk.

answer:
The first PT_PROF sweep printed nothing because the profiling build's Metal source failed to compile at runtime, so the binary exited before emitting any benchmark line — and my sweep command hid the reason by sending stderr to /dev/null.

Specifically: in the _prof copy I guarded the mesh-intersection shortcut as `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && pt_intersect_mesh(...))`, but the function I patched, pt_intersect_scene, has no local `params` — it reaches the parameters through the scene struct (`scene.params`). Since the shaders are compiled at startup by newLibraryWithSource, that undeclared identifier was a shader compile error, not a C++ one, so `clang++` reported only a warning and the build looked clean; the failure surfaced only when the program ran, as `metal init error: shader compile failed: program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'`. Because each run was wrapped as `... 2>/dev/null | tail -1`, the error text vanished and every PT_PROF line came back empty (#52). I diagnosed it by re-running one configuration directly with stderr shown (#53-54), fixed it to `scene.params->pad` (#55-56), and the same sweep then produced the cost shares: gpu_ms_best 45.352 full, 44.051 no shadow walk, 43.171 no NEE, 4.773 no mesh closest-hit, i.e. the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame (#58).
